correctness.rationale: The geodesic condition is quantified over all paths of length at most three. Every 2x2 tile holds at most 2 selected vertices; every 3x2 and 2x3 tile at most 3, with exactly two legal optimal triples; every 3x3 tile at most 5 by adjacent-column constraints. Tiling m=2a+3 epsilon and n=2b+3 delta gives the exact upper bound (mn+epsilon*delta)/2=ceil(mn/2). A parity class attains it. At width three, pairwise tile equality and the explicit forbidden phase-flip certify the unique/two optimizer counts. The proof is self-contained and includes edge cases m,n=2. Independent finite forbidden-triple generators (shortest-path enumeration and Manhattan-betweenness) agree, and all tested maxima satisfy the theorem; tests are not relied on for the infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The 2020 primary paper asks for general d-position numbers for grid graphs at d>=3; it gives the d=2/dissociation reduction and its even-by-even consequence, which are explicitly excluded from claims of novelty. The 2024 primary paper solves width-two grids for arbitrary k,d, and its Open Problems 7.1 singles out wider rectangular grids. The new mixed/odd-parity fixed d=3 formula for all grids of both widths >=3, plus the three-row optimizer rigidity, is neither stated nor implied by the inspected statements. Independent prior claims in local search concern matching complexes, multiset dimension of cylinders, or spider general-position polynomials, so their objects or invariants do not imply the theorem. The closest open-problem sources and published-finding corpus searches were compared semantically; a later unindexed equivalent remains possible.

value.rationale: The two cited primary papers explicitly motivate the finite-grid d>=3 problem and leave width >2 unresolved. The theorem settles the entire d=3, k=3 rectangular grid slice, including all mixed/odd sizes not supplied by existing even-even and two-row results, rather than a handpicked cutoff. Rigidity for the natural first wider strip gives an exact all-n extremal classification. The strict separation at 3x4 from the known d=2 value demonstrates the genuine new constraint.
